[LDET.3.3a.8] **One definition for a value computed both at compile time and at
runtime.** When the *same* logical value is computed in **two places** — once at
compile time (folded into the bundle) and once at runtime (recomputed by the
engine) — both computations **MUST** derive from a **single exact definition**,
so the two agree **bit-for-bit**. A value MUST NOT be carried in one
representation for the compile-time computation and a different,
independently-rounded representation for the runtime one; where a convenience
representation is stored (e.g. a `double` for display or interpolation), it MUST
NOT be an arithmetic input to either computation of the shared value. Two
derivations of "the same" value that can disagree by a ULP are a determinism
defect even when each is internally EXACT. *Instance:* a series window boundary
or a unit-conversion factor used **both** at compile time (folded into a lowered
atom) and at runtime (recomputed by the engine) must derive from a single exact
definition, so the two agree to the bit; a convenience `double` stored for
display must not be an arithmetic input to either computation.
